thread:
maria: gitleaks just flagged a GCP service-account JSON in infra/terraform. File path: terraform/remote/terraform.tfstate (commit 3f2a9b). Looks like the private_key blob was printed into the CI logs during 'apply'. :rotating_light:
alex: can you paste the private_key_id or key fingerprint? need to know if it's still valid.
maria: partial: private_key_id: abcdef1234567890, service_account: terraform-backend@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com. Detected in GH Actions runner actions-runner-21, job 'deploy'. cc @sam
devsec-bot: Automated detection: gitleaks v2.1 — SEVERITY: HIGH. Repo: infra/terraform. Path: .terraform/terraform.tfstate (exposed in logs). Commit: 3f2a9b. Fingerprint: sha256:7d4c... Recommendation: revoke key, rotate, scrub history, rotate CI secrets.
sam: Agreed. Immediate steps we should take (short):
  1) Revoke the key in GCP now:
     gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete "abcdef1234567890" --iam-account=terraform-backend@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-inference-prod
  2) Create new SA and grant least privilege (storage.objectAdmin for TF remote state only).
  3) Replace GH Actions secret (TF_BACKEND_KEY) with new key. Rotate any other places using it.
  4) Remove secret from git history: use git filter-repo or BFG, then force-push.
  5) Invalidate any CI caches and re-run affected jobs.
  6) Check Cloud Logging for any usage of the leaked key.

jordan: To check usage quickly:
  gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="terraform-backend@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com" AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.serviceAccountKeyName:"keys/abcdef1234567890"' --limit 50 --project=redwood-inference-prod
  Also check storage access: gsutil ls -a gs://redwood-tf-state/ --impersonate-service-account=terraform-backend@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com  (or query audit logs)
maria: FYI I just revoked the key (revoked at 2026-03-20T15:12:40Z). Created new SA with smaller scope (storage.objectAdmin) and updated the TF backend secret in repo settings. Forced a rotate of the Actions secret and kicked off a test apply. :white_check_mark:
sam: Please run git filter-repo to scrub the historical commit, then force-push. Reminder commands we usually use: 
  git filter-repo --path .terraform/terraform.tfstate --replace-text replacements.txt
  (or) java -jar bfg.jar --delete-files 'terraform.tfstate'
  after scrub: git push --force origin main
  We should also run repo-wide grep for 'private_key' and '-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----' to find other leaks.
devsec-bot: I've created an incident ticket SEC-2026-114 and added the detection rule to block plaintext 'private_key' in CI logs and to alert @eng-security. Also queued a repo scan across all infra repos.
jordan: Post-incident actions:
  - Enforce Workload Identity for GKE and avoid long-lived SA keys for CI.
  - Add KMS-encrypted TF state (CMEK) and restrict CMEK IAM.
  - Add pre-commit hook to block TF state files and SA JSON from being committed (also update our CONTRIBUTING docs).
  - Audit all service accounts for overly-broad roles; schedule RBAC cleanup ticket.
maria: I'll prepare a short retro and assign ownership to infra-security to track follow-ups. I've attached the list of affected commits and the forced-push SHA in the incident ticket.
sam: Also add a scheduled repo scan (weekly) for high-risk patterns and a GitHub Actions policy to redact logs containing 'private_key' or '-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----'.
maria: Thanks everyone. Closing action items: key revoked, new SA created, GH secret rotated, history scrub started, incident ticket SEC-2026-114 created. Will post the retro doc link once ready. :lock:
